LESSON: HEALING THE PARALYSED MAN

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: The Life of Jesus
Topic 3.5: Healing the Paralysed Man

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Healing the Paralysed Man. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why is the healing of the paralysed man significant to Christians today?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. describe the healing of the paralysed man

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE LEARNING: HEALING THE PARALYSED MAN
This lesson teaches Healing the Paralysed Man for Grade 5 CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION.

STUDY STEPS
1. describe the healing of the paralysed man
   Practise this until you can do it without help.

HOW TO SHOW UNDERSTANDING
Explain the idea in your own words, give one Kenyan example, then complete the practice tasks.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Describe Healing the Paralysed Man using something at your school.

Example 2: Give a home/community example from your county.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Underline the key ideas about Healing the Paralysed Man above.
2. Explain Healing the Paralysed Man to a parent using one local example.
3. Write or draw three things that prove you understand Healing the Paralysed Man.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Healing the Paralysed Man with school or home examples.
2. Answer: Why is Healing the Paralysed Man important for a Grade 5 learner?
3. Prepare a one-minute oral presentation for a parent or teacher.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is the healing of the paralysed man significant to Christians today?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. describe the healing of the paralysed man

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
